confidence_semantics: publisher/source authority only; not parcel numeric accuracy

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Coverage Metadata - Survey Data
verified_facts: EA publishes a dedicated Coverage Metadata - Survey Data dataset with WMS, WFS and OGC API Features service links.
This dataset is the service root for survey-index feature collections rather than an elevation raster itself.
semantic_limits: Coverage metadata is lineage/discovery evidence, not a terrain measurement.
A parcel-specific survey remains unresolved until an exact feature match is made.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey index OGC API Features landing page
verified_facts: EA exposes an unauthenticated OGC API Features 1.0 landing page for survey-index files.
The landing page links to machine-readable API, collections and conformance documents.
semantic_limits: Service availability does not by itself identify the survey used at a target parcel.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey index OGC API feature collections
verified_facts: The official collections document lists Composite 1m DTM, Time Stamped DTM, point-cloud and National LIDAR Programme index collections.
The listed LiDAR collections use EPSG:27700 storage CRS and expose queryables plus GeoJSON/GML/CSV-compatible feature output.
semantic_limits: Collection presence is not a spatial match; exact feature filtering remains required.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite 1m DTM 2022 extents collection
verified_facts: The collection is stored in EPSG:27700 and exposes filename, tilename, polygon_id, resolution, year, source DTM filename and flown-date fields.
The collection exposes geometry for spatial filtering.
semantic_limits: A tile-name or record match must be spatially validated before being promoted to parcel lineage.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite 1m DTM queryables
verified_facts: Official queryables include filename, tilename, polygon_id, resolution, year, od_dtm_fn, sd_flown and ed_flown.
These fields support explicit survey-source and acquisition-date QA instead of filename inference.
semantic_limits: Queryable field availability is not evidence that any particular target has matched a feature.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Extents collection
verified_facts: The time-stamped DTM feature schema includes survey name, DTM name, OS tile, survey dates, season, polygon id, resolution, transform and geoid.
The collection is stored in EPSG:27700.
semantic_limits: Time-stamped records remain provenance candidates until spatially intersected with the exact target geometry.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Extents queryables
verified_facts: Official queryables expose lidar_name, dtm_name, ostilename, osgrid, start/end flown dates, year, season, polygonid, resolution, returns, area_sqkm, transform, geoid, archived, supplied and latest.
Transform and geoid can therefore be validated from the actual feature rather than assumed globally.
semantic_limits: No transform/geoid value is assigned to the three target parcels until a real feature match succeeds.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Ground Truth Surveys
verified_facts: EA describes independently surveyed ground-truth points with approximately +/-3cm RMSE and attributes including date, surface type, method, transform and geoidal model.
EA compares timestamped LiDAR surveys with ground-truth data and requires less than +/-15cm RMSE plus 10cm standard-deviation/random-error limits to pass QC.
semantic_limits: Ground-truth point accuracy is independent QC context and must not be copied to parcel raster uncertainty.
A ground-truth survey may support multiple LiDAR surveys and must be matched explicitly.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Ground Truth Surveys OGC API Features
verified_facts: EA exposes a separate unauthenticated OGC API Features endpoint for LIDAR Ground Truth Surveys.
The endpoint links to API, collections and conformance resources.
semantic_limits: Ground-truth service availability does not prove a matching QC survey exists for a target parcel.

candidates.name: LIDAR Tiles Catalogues ArcGIS FeatureServer
verified_facts: The official FeatureServer exposes DTM and DSM Time Stamped Extents layers in EPSG:27700 and supports JSON queries.
It is retained as a cross-check/discovery route alongside the newer OGC API service.
semantic_limits: Legacy service results must not override the current OGC API or exact spatial-match requirements.

candidates.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Extents FeatureServer layer
verified_facts: The layer description says it represents unique survey extents with capture date, DTM resolution and transformation models.
Fields include filename, OS reference, flown dates, point count/spacing, returns, classification, transform, geoid, year, supplied/latest and polygon id.
semantic_limits: Schema agreement improves lineage validation but does not itself identify the target survey.

candidates.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons spatial data guidance
verified_facts: HMLR describes INSPIRE polygons as showing position and indicative extent of registered freehold property and links each polygon through a Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
The files are supplied as GML for use in GIS.
semantic_limits: INSPIRE remains indicative horizontal geometry and is not a determined legal boundary or terrain measurement.
